name: United Arab Emirates
headline_status: Cannabis is illegal in the UAE, and personal use can bring prison, heavy fines and deportation for foreigners.
summary: The UAE's narcotics law, Federal Decree-Law No. 30 of 2021, punishes unauthorised personal drug use with at least three months in prison or a fine of AED 20,000 to 100,000, with harsher penalties for repeat offences and trafficking. Foreigners convicted must generally be deported. Since 2024 a Cabinet resolution sets administrative fines, and for repeat cases deportation and entry bans, for non-resident visitors caught with small quantities at entry points. Users who seek treatment before an arrest order can avoid prosecution.

penalties.value: Unauthorised personal use of scheduled drugs carries a minimum of three months in prison or a fine of AED 20,000 to 100,000; repeat offences raise the penalty, and trafficking can carry the death penalty in aggravated cases.

possession_limit.value: No legal amount; any unauthorised possession or use is an offence.

regulator.value: Governed by Federal Decree-Law No. 30 of 2021 on narcotics and psychotropic substances, amended by Federal Decree-Law No. 53 of 2023.

tourists.value: Cabinet Resolution No. 43 of 2024 lets non-resident visitors caught with small quantities at entry points be fined (from AED 5,000 for a first offence for some substances), with deportation and entry bans for repeat or more serious cases. Foreigners convicted in court must generally be deported.

timeline.event: Federal Decree-Law No. 30 of 2021 replaces the 1995 narcotics law
Federal Decree-Law No. 53 of 2023 amends the narcotics law
Cabinet Resolution No. 43 sets administrative penalties for non-resident visitors caught with small amounts at entry points

faq.q: Is weed legal in Dubai or the UAE?
faq.a: No. Personal use is punishable by at least three months in prison or a fine of AED 20,000 to 100,000.

faq.q: What happens to tourists caught with cannabis in the UAE?
faq.a: Non-resident visitors caught with small amounts at entry points can be fined under a 2024 Cabinet resolution, and repeat or serious cases bring deportation and entry bans. Foreigners convicted in court are generally deported.

faq.q: Can drug users in the UAE avoid prosecution by seeking treatment?
faq.a: Yes, if the user, a relative or guardian requests treatment before an arrest order is issued and any drugs are handed over. Treatment lasts up to one year.
